system_prompt:
You are an eighth-grade student taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in your grade. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
Katy made a table to keep track of how long it took water in a beaker to cool from 95°C to 70°C. She measured the time it took the water to cool in 5°C intervals.

| Interval Readings | Amount of Cooling Time |
| :--- | :--- |
| 95°C – 90°C | 2 minutes 10 seconds |
| 90°C – 85°C | 3 minutes 19 seconds |
| 85°C – 80°C | 4 minutes 48 seconds |
| 80°C – 75°C | 6 minutes 55 seconds |
| 75°C – 70°C | 9 minutes 43 seconds |

Estimate to the nearest minute the total time taken for the temperature of the water in the beaker to cool from 95°C to 70°C, and explain how your estimate was made.

Estimate: ____

Explain:

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Estimate: 27 minutes. Explanation: I rounded each interval time to the nearest minute, then added them. 2 min 10 s rounds to 2 minutes (10 s is less than 30 s). 3 min 19 s rounds to 3 minutes (19 s is less than 30 s). 4 min 48 s rounds to 5 minutes (48 s is more than 30 s). 6 min 55 s rounds to 7 minutes (55 s is more than 30 s). 9 min 43 s rounds to 10 minutes (43 s is more than 30 s). Adding the rounded values: 2 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 10 = 27 minutes.
